summary:
I checked all three LEFT findings against the code. All three were real, and all three are fixed. None rejected.

LEFT-R1 (a cancelled group could be re-locked and then submitted): confirmed. POST /:code/lock now uses a conditional updateMany (status 'open' and orderId null → 'locked'). Anything else gets 422 GROUP_LOCKED "Group is <status>". So a cancelled group, a submitted group or an already-locked group can no longer be locked. Submit now closes the cart with a conditional updateMany too (open or locked, orderId null → locked). If that matches nothing it re-reads the group and answers alreadySubmitted, GROUP_CANCELLED or GROUP_LOCKED, so a cancel that gets in first wins. Regression test: cancel → lock gives 422 and status stays 'cancelled' → submit gives 422 GROUP_CANCELLED, and no order exists for group-CANCL1.

LEFT-R2 (a refused submit strands a locked cart): confirmed. I took option (a): lock and submit are one server step. Submit closes the cart itself, then reads the items after closing it. The hours check, section check, priceOrder and ingestOrder (which raises ITEM_NOT_PRICED) are each wrapped in a guard. If one refuses and no order exists with external id group-<code>, the guard moves the group from locked back to open. The NO_ITEMS refusal reopens the group too. A group locked earlier through /lock is also reopened when its submit is refused, which frees groups already stuck that way. On the page I removed the separate /lock call and the client menu pre-check. It now makes one submit call and shows the server's message. For ITEM_UNAVAILABLE and ITEM_NOT_PRICED it adds "Whoever added it can remove it, then send the group again", and that is now true because the group is open. The page then reloads the menu and the open/closed line. The button reads "Send group order". It stays enabled for open and locked groups, which is safe because the server accepts both.

LEFT-R3 (the client-side Total left out the service charge and item tax classes): confirmed. GET /group-orders/:code now returns quote = { tender, itemTotalCents, taxCents, serviceChargeCents, totalCents }. It comes from the same priceOrder(lines, 'cash', 'group', concept) call submit makes; a shared groupLines() helper builds the lines for both. It is null when the cart is empty or the group is submitted. The concept fields in that response are now id, name, slug, tenantId, taxRateCash, taxRateCard; the legacy taxRate was dropped. The page no longer computes tax. It shows the server's Subtotal and Tax, a Service charge line when it is above zero, the Total, and the note "Tax at the cash rate. Paying by card is re-priced at the till." Test: a company whose service charge is 10% on pos, with a cart that includes a zero-rated item. The quote is itemTotal 275,000, tax 40,500, service charge 31,550, total 347,050, and the submit total equals the quote total.

Residual race I left alone. The add-item route checks for 'open' and then inserts without a transaction. An add that passed its check just before submit closes the cart can therefore land after submit has read the items, and that item would not be on the order. The window is milliseconds. Closing it would need a transaction or row lock in the add route.
tests: cd /home/user/servd/backend && DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/servd_test_left_build REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/30 JWT_SECRET=... JWT_REFRESH_SECRET=... NODE_ENV=test npx vitest run tests/groupOrderSubmit.test.ts → 13/13 passed. 5 tests are new: R1 cancel→lock→submit; R1 lock only moves an open group (lock twice gives 422, a locked group still submits, a submitted group never re-locks); R2 refused submit → remove the line → submit works; R2 a group locked earlier is reopened when its submit is refused; R3 quote equals the submit total with service charge and a zero-rated item. 2 existing tests now also assert the group is 'open' after a refused submit (ITEM_UNAVAILABLE, ITEM_NOT_PRICED). The 'prisma:error Unique constraint' line in the double-tap test's output is ingestOrder's own concurrent-insert handling; the test passes. tsc --noEmit: backend 0 errors (tsconfig includes src only), frontend/storefront 0 errors. No next build or dev was run.
needsOtherFiles: None. Nothing outside groupOrders, the page and the test calls /group-orders/:code/lock (mobile, tablet and admin were grepped), so the stricter lock breaks no caller. The mobile app has no group-order client.
deviations: For R2 I chose the reviewer's option (a): lock and submit in one step, with the group reopened when a guard refuses. I did not add an /unlock route. The client menu pre-check is removed rather than tightened, because the server's answer no longer strands the cart. GET /:code no longer returns concept.taxRate (legacy 17%, which CLAUDE.md says never to use) and now returns tenantId and taxRateCard, which the quote needs; the public /storefront/concepts already exposes tenantId. The POST /:code/lock route is kept for any explicit lock, but only from 'open'. The cancel route is unchanged: if a cancel lands mid-submit after the order has been created, the final claim marks the group 'submitted' with the real orderId.
